call.heart_attack.0: It's my husband — he's clutching his chest and sweating, says his left arm has gone numb. Please hurry!
call.heart_attack.1: My father went grey at the dinner table. Pain in his chest, he can hardly breathe. He's sixty-two.
call.stroke.0: Mum's speech is slurred and one side of her face is drooping. She can't lift her right arm!
call.stroke.1: My colleague suddenly can't talk properly and keeps dropping things. Half his face isn't moving.
call.childbirth.0: My wife's waters just broke, the contractions are three minutes apart and we have no car!
call.childbirth.1: My neighbour is in labour and her husband is on a night shift. She's screaming that the baby is coming.
call.child_fever.0: My son is burning up — forty degrees, and he just had a fit. He's two years old.
call.child_fever.1: My baby won't stop crying, she's very hot and there's a strange rash on her tummy.
call.diabetic.0: My brother is diabetic. He's shaking, sweating and talking nonsense. We can't find his sugar.
call.diabetic.1: An old man in our stairwell is confused and pale. There's an insulin pen in his pocket.
call.allergy.0: We're at a wedding — a guest ate something with nuts, his face is swelling and he's wheezing!
call.allergy.1: A wasp stung my daughter and now her lips are swelling. She says her throat feels tight.
call.elderly_fall.0: My grandmother fell in the bathroom. She's conscious but can't stand up, her hip hurts badly.
call.elderly_fall.1: Our elderly neighbour slipped on the stairs. He's sitting up, but his wrist looks broken.
call.drowning.0: Someone fell into the canal! People pulled him out, but he isn't breathing properly!
call.drowning.1: A teenager jumped off the bridge for a dare and didn't come up straight away. He's out now — his lips are blue!
call.wedding_poisoning.0: Half the guests at our wedding are vomiting after the plov! At least eight people, two have fainted.
call.wedding_poisoning.1: After the birthday party the whole family has terrible stomach cramps. Grandma and the little ones are the worst.
call.asthma.0: My son is having an asthma attack and his inhaler is empty. His lips are turning blue!
call.asthma.1: My aunt can't catch her breath — she's wheezing, bent forward, can't finish a sentence.
call.unconscious_party.0: A guy at the party collapsed and won't wake up. His friends say he 'took something'.
call.unconscious_party.1: A young man is lying in our courtyard. He doesn't respond and he's breathing very slowly.
call.kitchen_burn.0: My wife spilled boiling oil on her arm while cooking. The skin is blistering badly.
call.kitchen_burn.1: The kettle tipped over onto my little girl's leg. She's crying, the skin is red and peeling.
call.apartment_fire.0: Fire on the fourth floor! Black smoke from the window, people are shouting from the balconies!
call.apartment_fire.1: The flat next door is on fire — the stairwell is full of smoke, we can't get down!
call.kitchen_fire.0: The frying pan caught fire and now the cupboards are burning! I can't put it out!
call.kitchen_fire.1: Smoke is pouring out of our neighbour's kitchen window and nobody answers the door.
call.car_fire.0: A parked car is on fire in our courtyard. Flames under the bonnet, and other cars are right next to it.
call.car_fire.1: A car just burst into flames at the traffic lights! The driver got out, but it's spreading.
call.trash_fire.0: The rubbish skip behind our building is burning and the smoke is coming in through the windows.
call.trash_fire.1: Someone set fire to a pile of rubbish by the bus stop. The wind is pushing it towards the trees.
call.gas_leak.0: There's a strong smell of gas in our stairwell. Nobody knows which flat it's coming from!
call.gas_leak.1: I came home and the whole flat smells of gas. I haven't touched a single light switch.
call.bazaar_fire.0: Fire at the Bazaar! The fabric stalls are burning and it's spreading from row to row!
call.bazaar_fire.1: Night guard at the Bazaar here. The spice warehouse is on fire and the roof is going!
call.tandir_roof.0: Sparks from the neighbour's tandir landed on the roof — the old wooden roof is burning!
call.tandir_roof.1: We were baking bread in the yard and the reed canopy caught fire. It's spreading to the house!
call.decoy_transformer.0: Factory night watchman here. The transformer by the gate is sparking and smoking, there's a smell of burning cable.
call.decoy_transformer.1: Something blew up in the electrical cabinet at the plant. Cables are burning and the lights are out.
call.decoy_petrol_station.0: Filling station attendant. A driver pulled away with the nozzle still in — there's petrol all over the forecourt!
call.decoy_petrol_station.1: A tanker is leaking petrol at our filling station. The smell is awful — one cigarette and it's over!
call.decoy_garage_heater.0: Our garage is on fire — my husband left the electric heater on while he was working on the car.
call.decoy_garage_heater.1: Smoke from my neighbour's garage. He keeps an old heater in there; I think it's caught fire.
call.burglary.0: Someone is breaking into the flat next door — I can hear the lock being forced. The owners are away.
call.burglary.1: There's a man in my garden with a torch, trying the windows one by one. I'm alone with the kids.
call.street_fight.0: A big fight outside the café! Five or six men, and one of them has a bottle!
call.street_fight.1: Two groups are fighting at the bus stop. People are getting knocked to the ground.
call.domestic.0: My neighbour is beating his wife again. She's screaming and things are breaking.
call.domestic.1: My stepfather is drunk and threatening my mum with a knife. I've locked myself in the bathroom.
call.car_theft.0: Two guys are trying the doors of every car in our yard. One just got into a black Nexia.
call.car_theft.1: Someone is taking the wheels off my car right now — I can see them from the window.
call.drunk_driver.0: A car is swerving all over the avenue and nearly hit a pedestrian. The driver looks drunk.
call.drunk_driver.1: A Cobalt with no lights on is racing down the wrong side of the road.
call.armed_robbery.0: We're being robbed — the all-night shop! Two men with a gun, they're still inside!
call.armed_robbery.1: Masked men just held up the currency exchange on the corner. They're loading a car!
call.missing_child.0: My six-year-old didn't come home from the playground. It's dark, we've looked everywhere!
call.missing_child.1: My daughter is twelve. She went to a friend's at seven and her phone is off. The friend never saw her.
call.loud_party.0: It's two in the morning and the neighbours are blasting music. I have to be at work at seven!
call.loud_party.1: A wedding in the courtyard has been going since ten — drums, fireworks, nobody can sleep.
call.vandalism.0: Teenagers are smashing the glass of the bus shelter. They're still here.
call.vandalism.1: Someone is spray-painting the school wall and kicking the parked cars.
call.car_crash.0: Two cars crashed at the crossroads! One driver is bleeding from the head and people are fighting.
call.car_crash.1: A car hit a taxi — the taxi driver is trapped behind the wheel, and the other driver is trying to leave!
call.crash_fire.0: A car hit a pole and the engine is on fire! The driver is still inside and he isn't moving!
call.crash_fire.1: A minibus has overturned and there's smoke from the engine. Passengers are hurt, someone is trapped!
call.stabbing.0: A man has been stabbed outside the bar! He's bleeding heavily — the attacker ran towards the park!
call.stabbing.1: A robbery — they stabbed the cashier and ran. He's on the floor holding his side.
call.gas_explosion.0: An explosion in our building — the whole stairwell shook! Gas, I think. Fire on the second floor and people are hurt!
call.gas_explosion.1: A gas cylinder exploded in a ground-floor café. Windows blown out, fire, people lying on the pavement!
call.hit_and_run.0: A car hit a pedestrian and drove off! The man is lying in the road, conscious but bleeding.
call.hit_and_run.1: A motorbike knocked down a girl at the crossing and sped away. She can't get up.
call.smoke_grandpa.0: Grandpa fell and he isn't getting up! Oh, and there's smoke coming from the kitchen, I don't know why...
call.smoke_grandpa.1: My grandmother fainted in the bedroom. It's so smoky in here I can hardly see her!
call.co_poisoning.0: Everyone in our flat has a terrible headache and keeps falling asleep. The gas heater's been on all night...
call.co_poisoning.1: My parents won't wake up properly — dizzy and sick. We sealed the windows against the cold and lit the stove.
call.scream_noise.0: Just a noise complaint... the neighbours are shouting. Wait — now a woman is screaming 'help, he's bleeding'!
call.scream_noise.1: Loud banging upstairs. I thought it was a party, but someone keeps crying 'stop, you'll kill him'.
call.engine_running.0: A car has been parked outside with the engine running for an hour. The man inside isn't moving. Drunk, probably.
call.engine_running.1: A suspicious man is slumped over in a car by the school. He doesn't react when I knock on the glass.
call.balcony_child.0: A toddler is climbing the railing of a fifth-floor balcony! The parents are out and the door is locked!
call.balcony_child.1: A little boy is hanging on the outside of a sixth-floor balcony! Nobody can get into the flat!
call.tree_on_car.0: The wind brought a huge tree down on a car! The driver is trapped inside, he's moaning.
call.tree_on_car.1: A poplar fell on a taxi at the stop. The roof is crushed and the passenger is bleeding.
call.power_line.0: A power line is down across the road and sparking! The puddle around it is sizzling.
call.power_line.1: The storm snapped a pole — live wires are hanging over the pavement and the fence is smoking.
call.flooded_underpass.0: A car is stuck in the flooded underpass! Water up to the windows, people are standing on the roof!
call.flooded_underpass.1: A minibus stalled in the flooded tunnel. Water is pouring in and an old woman can't climb out!
call.roof_sheet.0: A metal roof sheet flew off and hit a man in the street! He has a deep cut on his head.
call.roof_sheet.1: The wind blew a shop window onto a passer-by. There's glass everywhere and a lot of blood.
call.fan_brawl.0: The derby fans are fighting outside the stadium gates! Dozens of them, bottles flying!
call.fan_brawl.1: Away fans are smashing car windows on the stadium road and attacking anyone in a red scarf.
call.crowd_crush.0: Crush at Gate 3! Everyone pushed for the exit, people are falling, someone isn't breathing!
call.crowd_crush.1: The barrier in the stand collapsed! People are piled on top of each other and children are crying!
call.pickpocket.0: My wallet and phone were stolen at the stadium exit. I can still see the guy — red cap!
call.pickpocket.1: A gang of pickpockets is working the crowd at the stadium bus stop. They just robbed an old man.
call.flare_smoke.0: Smoke and fire by the stadium! Red flames in the stands... wait, they're flares — and they're fighting, a man is down!
call.flare_smoke.1: Fire in the stadium car park! Well, flares... someone threw one into the crowd, a woman's face is burned and the fans are brawling.
call.prank_ufo.0: Hello, police? A UFO just landed at the Bazaar! It's green and... (stifled laughter) ...it wants plov.
call.prank_ufo.1: Aliens are abducting my neighbour's cow! Send everyone! (giggling; someone whispers 'go on, say it!')
call.prank_lion.0: A lion has escaped from the zoo and it's in my yard! A real lion! (a TV is blaring in the background)
call.prank_lion.1: There's a tiger on the circus roof! Come quickly! (laughter, loud music)
call.prank_pizza.0: Hi, one large pizza with extra cheese, please... What? This is 112? Oh. Sorry.
call.prank_pizza.1: Is this the taxi company? I need a car to the airport at five... No? Then who are you?
call.prank_dare.0: My house is on fire! Bet you can't get here in five minutes! (a group laughing, someone is filming)
call.prank_dare.1: Fire! Everything's burning! ...Ha, see? I told you I'd do it! (laughter, the line goes dead)
call.prank_shashlik.0: Smoke and flames in the yard next door! ...And it smells of grilled meat. And they're singing.
call.prank_shashlik.1: There's a fire in my neighbour's yard! They're dancing round it... is that a barbecue? Yes — it's shashlik.
call.prank_cat.0: My cat has been stuck up a tree since the evening. She won't stop meowing. Can you send the firemen?
call.prank_cat.1: Our cat climbed onto the neighbour's garage roof and won't come down. My daughter can't sleep.
call.prank_wifi.0: My internet has been down for three hours! Who am I supposed to call? Arrest the provider!
call.prank_wifi.1: The neighbours changed their Wi-Fi password and won't tell me the new one. That's theft, isn't it?
call.karim_lonely.0: Hello, dear, it's Karim-bobo again. No, nothing happened... I just couldn't sleep. How are you?
call.karim_lonely.1: Karim-bobo here. Is it raining where you are? My grandchildren never call... I won't keep you long.
call.karim_lonely.2: It's Karim-bobo. I made too much soup today. Do you dispatchers ever eat at night? (chuckles)
call.karim_heart.0: It's Karim-bobo... sorry to bother you again... (heavy breathing) my chest... it's squeezing, like a stone on it...
call.jasur_prank.0: Fire! Fire at the school! ...Ha-ha, got you! (the same boy's voice as last night)
call.jasur_prank.1: Hello? A bomb— no, a bear! There's a bear at the school! (snorting with laughter, hangs up)
call.jasur_prank.2: This is an emergency: my teacher is too strict! Send the police! (his friends cheering)
call.jasur_real.0: It's Jasur... I know, I know, but this time it's REAL! The school gym is on fire, the alarm is ringing — please!
call.botir_gas.0: Botir from the bakery here. There's a smell of gas by the ovens — I've switched everything off, but it's strong.
call.botir_breakin.0: Botir the baker again. Someone's breaking down the back door of my bakery — I can hear them inside!
call.botir_van.0: It's Botir. The storm brought a tree down on my delivery van — my driver is pinned and the engine is smoking!
call.botir_petrol.0: Botir here, on my bread round in the Industrial Zone. A man in a grey jacket with a petrol can is hanging around the warehouses. He saw me, smiled and said: 'Hurry — or you'll be late again.'
call.arson_warehouse.0: A warehouse in the Industrial Zone is burning. It smells of petrol. (a calm male voice) Hurry — or you'll be late again.
call.arson_warehouse.1: Fire at the timber warehouse in the Industrial Zone. Strong smell of petrol. (the same calm voice) Hurry — or you'll be late again.
call.arson_kiosk.0: The kiosk by the factory gates is on fire. Petrol everywhere. (calm, almost amused) Hurry — or you'll be late again.
call.arson_kiosk.1: A newspaper kiosk in the Industrial Zone is in flames. You can smell the petrol from here. Hurry — or you'll be late again.
call.arson_garage.0: The garages behind the plant are burning. Petrol, black smoke. (a calm voice) Hurry — or you'll be late again.
call.arson_garage.1: A row of garages in the Industrial Zone is on fire — someone poured petrol under the doors. Hurry — or you'll be late again.
call.arson_finale.0: The big warehouse in the Industrial Zone is burning — the last one. Petrol, of course. (the calm voice, slower now) Hurry — or you'll be late again. For the last time.
call.finale_decoy.0: Fire at the Bazaar! The fruit stalls by the main gate are burning! People saw a man running away!
hint.smoke: Smoke is mentioned — a fire crew is probably needed as well.
hint.co: Headaches and drowsiness next to a gas heater: suspect carbon monoxide — fire crew and ambulance.
hint.scream: Someone is screaming about bleeding — send an ambulance as well as the police.
hint.unconscious: Not drunk: a driver who doesn't respond is a medical emergency.
hint.ladder: A rescue at height needs a fire crew with a ladder, not a patrol car.
hint.flare: Flares, not a fire: there are injuries and a fight — ambulance and police.
hint.laugh: Laughter in the background; this number has false calls on record.
hint.zoo: Yangiobod has no zoo, and the circus left town in the spring.
hint.nonemergency: Not an emergency — no unit needed. Dismiss it politely.
hint.shashlik: Smoke, music and grilled meat at night: a barbecue, not a fire.
hint.karim: Karim-bobo, a lonely pensioner who calls most nights just to talk.
hint.karim_heart: Karim-bobo — but he is short of breath. This time it is chest pain.
hint.jasur: Jasur, fourteen — a known prankster. Same number, same giggles.
hint.jasur_real: Jasur's number — but no laughter, and a fire alarm is ringing behind him.
hint.petrol: Petrol in the Industrial Zone again — Inspector Dilshod asked us to flag these (F).
hint.finale: Dilshod's stakeout is right there. Police and fire together.
tip.title: Zuhra-opa
tip.welcome: Welcome, child. Thirty years I've sat in this chair, and Friday is my last night. Calls appear on the left. Read every one carefully — people in trouble don't always say what they need. Space pauses the clock if you need a breath.
tip.first_call: A call! Select it with ↑/↓ and read the text below. Press number keys 1–9 to pick units (A — ambulance, F — fire engine, P — police), then Enter to send them. The nearest free unit is usually the right one.
tip.prank: Hear that? Not every call is real. Pranks and calls that aren't emergencies — dismiss them with D. But careful: dismissing a real emergency is the worst thing you can do in this chair.
tip.multi: Some calls need more than one service — a crash with injuries needs an ambulance and the police. Pick several units before you press Enter.
tip.escalation: A call left waiting gets worse. Severity rises, and once it's critical (!!!) the clock is running — if nobody arrives in time, we lose them.
tip.report: Crews radio back what they find. If you sent the wrong service, the report tells you what's really needed — send it, and quickly.
tip.arson: Petrol, the Industrial Zone, and that calm voice... It isn't the first one. Inspector Dilshod asked us to flag calls like this: select it and press F. He reviews our flags after every shift.
tip.stress: You're tense, I can see it. Once a shift you can take a coffee break with C — I'll cover the phones for fifteen minutes. The city won't love it, but burning out is worse.
briefing.0: Monday. This is our Yangiobod: the hospital (H) is in the north-west, the fire station (F) just south of the river, the police (P) in the north-east. Four bridges cross the river — remember them. I'll be right here beside you.
briefing.1: Tuesday. You survived Monday, and so did the city. Tonight will be busier. And don't forget the petrol smell — Dilshod is counting on us.
briefing.2: Wednesday. A storm is coming: the roads are slow and the Bazaar bridge is flooded, so units will take the long way round. Trees, wires, water... look after yourself.
briefing.3: Thursday. Derby night at the stadium. After the final whistle a patrol car will be worth its weight in gold — and so will patience. Karim-bobo sounded unwell this morning, by the way.
briefing.4: Friday. My last shift. I won't tell you anything new — you already know it all. Just listen to the people on the line.
briefing.trap: Inspector Dilshod: "Thanks to your flags, my men are watching the warehouses in the Industrial Zone. If he strikes tonight, he'll try to distract you first. Police AND fire — to the right address."
briefing.notrap: Inspector Dilshod: "Not enough evidence for a stakeout. If he strikes again tonight, all we can do is put out the fire."
zuhra.title: Zuhra-opa
zuhra.S: Flawless. I haven't seen a shift like that since... well, since mine. Don't let it go to your head.
zuhra.A: Very good. A couple of rough edges, but the city slept safely tonight because of you.
zuhra.B: Solid work. Not perfect — but nobody here is. Tomorrow, be quicker on the critical ones.
zuhra.C: We lost time tonight, and sometimes more than time. Read carefully, send the nearest unit, and don't hesitate.
zuhra.D: A hard night. Go home, sleep, and come back ready. The city needs you at your best — and so do I.
zuhra.farewell: So that's it — my last shift is over. Thirty years... The headset is yours now. Look after this city, child.
zuhra.akmal: Captain Akmal grumbled again about his engines being sent the wrong way. Read the fire calls twice.
insp.title: Inspector Dilshod
insp.review: Tonight you flagged {flagged} calls: {correct} fit the pattern, {wrong} didn't.
insp.missed: Pattern calls you didn't flag tonight: {missed}.
insp.total: So far: {correct} correct, {wrong} false. For a trap I need {need} solid ones by Thursday — and no more false flags than correct ones.
insp.none: No flags tonight? Petrol, the Industrial Zone, a warehouse, a kiosk or a garage — and that phrase. Keep your ears open.
insp.ready: That's enough. If this holds, I set the trap for Friday night.
insp.not_ready_final: Not enough to set a trap. If he strikes on Friday, he'll walk away.
insp.too_many_false: Too many false flags. My people can't chase every barbecue in town.
insp.caught: We got him: a night watchman with a grudge against the whole Industrial Zone. Your flags put the handcuffs on him.
insp.escaped: He slipped away. The trap was set, but we were a minute too late.
insp.notrap_end: Another warehouse burned on Friday. Without a trap we could only watch. Maybe next time.
upgrade.extra_ambulance.desc: One more ambulance at the hospital.
upgrade.field_post.desc: An ambulance stationed by the railway station, south of the river.
upgrade.extra_fire.desc: One more engine at the fire station.
upgrade.extra_police.desc: One more police car at the station.
upgrade.screening.desc: A screening hint under each call: pranks, hidden injuries, hidden fires.
upgrade.green_wave.desc: Traffic lights turn green for sirens: every unit is 15% faster.
upgrade.rapid_triage.desc: Ambulance crews finish on scene 20% faster.
ending.e1.text: Friday, 06:00. Zuhra-opa takes off her headset and puts it in your hands — the old golden one from the day the centre opened. Inspector Dilshod brings tea and the morning paper: ARSONIST CAUGHT. Every night this week, the city was in good hands. Yours.
ending.e2.text: You made it through the week. Every call was answered, and the city held. Somewhere in the Industrial Zone a man in a grey jacket is still out there — but tonight Yangiobod sleeps, and Zuhra-opa leaves knowing her chair is in steady hands.
ending.e3.text: The arsonist is behind bars, and the papers are calling you the 'night detective'. But the week had its rough shifts, and Zuhra-opa's farewell is a little quieter than it might have been. 'You have the ear,' she says. 'Now get the speed.'
ending.e4.text: The city stopped trusting the voice on 112. In the morning the head of the centre asks for your badge. Zuhra-opa walks you to the door: 'Not everyone is made for this chair. There's no shame in that.'
ending.e5.text: The phones won't stop. Your hands are shaking and the screen swims. You take off the headset and walk out in the middle of the shift. Zuhra-opa takes your seat without a word. Some nights are stronger than we are.
